segments.text: The purpose of this video is to explain to you the proper assembly and disassembly of the Bueno Pump L8 drive.
The following tools will be needed to disassemble and assemble the pump.
First, you will need a 916-pound wrench on a 1 1⁄2-inch drive socket or equivalent.
You will need a large pipe wrench. You will need a 3⁄8-inch drive ratchet with a 3⁄4-inch drive socket.
a leveraged pipe for the pipe wrench and a crow's foot bar for aligning the drive pin,
which will be shown later.
The first step in removing the stator and the rotor from the housing is to remove this
set plug for the drive pin.
Screw the hold down plug out, go to the other side, remove this plug with your alignment
tool, remove the pin, lightly tap on it. This is the drive pin for the connecting rod.
Next step will be to remove these cap screws with your 3-8 drive, 3-quarter inch socket.
Remove the cap screws and the cap. I would suggest that you put a mark either on this
side of the cap or this side of the cap to ensure that this cap is put in place in
the same position as you removed. The next step would be to remove the stator and the
rotor as one piece from the actual housing. In order to do that you will need a large
pipe wrench. Once you have secured your pipe wrench tightly to the stator it is most likely
that you're going to need a leverage bar pipe to go over your pipe wrench in order
to unscrew the stator and the rotor from the housing. As I explained to you earlier, once
you put your pipe wrench in place, use your leverage pipe on the pipe wrench to remove
the stator and rotor from the housing. This at times can be very tight in the beginning,
but naturally because it's a pipe threat, will loosen up quickly. So once you get
of broke loose as you will see it will turn quite easily.
You can see I'm now removing it from the housing.
It's beginning to turn easily.
Once you have reached this point you're going to need a helper to slide the stator and rotor
out of the housing assembly to naturally set it on the ground.
Okay we're now prepared to remove the stator and the rotor from the housing assembly.
I've got my friend here, Rick, he's going to help you remove it.
We're going to set it out on the floor and I'm going to show you the seal on the end
of the connecting rod that should be on the end of the rod when you remove the assembly.
This connecting rod washer is very important in order to seal the water from getting into
the main shaft cavity.
If that washer is defective or is not in place when you reassemble it, you will cause corrosion
in this end and on this pin, which means you most likely won't get this pin out over time.
And you'll have water seepage around this collar and out these plugs.
